title: Adjoining one two-term localization factor to ordered coordinates
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number and f:Fin(r+1) to A a list. Work with module sheaves on the one-object bottom-topology ring site [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]. Let K be any nonnegative augmented integer cochain complex K to A[0]. Suppose K has degree-zero coordinate e0, positive ordered localization coordinates e, face A-algebra maps l and the diagonal, alternating differential and augmentation equations for the tail i maps to f(i+1), exactly as in the coordinate part of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]. Let P be the actual two-term complex [A to A[1/f(0)]] of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-extended-cech], and let b:P tensor K to A[0] be the tensor of the two augmentations followed by the left unitor. Then the positive terms of P tensor K admit ordered localization coordinates e and face A-algebra maps for the full list f. Its first differential has coordinates the diagonal localization of the actual degree-zero augmentation value b(x), and its later differential has the alternating face-sum coordinates. No degree-zero equivalence or assertion that b is a degree-zero isomorphism is part of this conclusion. This statement treats one tensor operation, assumes all tail coordinates, and makes no assertion about recursively tensoring an arbitrary list or about negative-degree terms.

proof.text: Apply the evaluated two-row tensor lemma to obtain the actual tensor complex degree-zero coordinate z, positive block coordinates c_q, and the augmentation and differential matrix equations. This lemma uses no generating list or ordered coordinates.

Combine the supplied e0 and e_q into degreewise equivalences C_n from the evaluated tail to the algebraic ordered tail terms. Conjugate each tail differential D_n by C_n to define d_n. The supplied hd0 and hd prove the diagonal and alternating formulas for d_n. Apply the algebraic localization-cone coordinate lemma to obtain E_q and the full face algebra maps.

Tensor C_n with the identity on S, take its product with C_(n+1), and compose this equivalence with c_q and E_q. Prove tensor naturality for the conjugated differential by induction on tensors, using d_n(C_n x)=C_(n+1)(D_n x). The block equations then give the full alternating differential. At the first differential use the block formula, the diagonal formula for E_0, and ha together with b(x)=a(z(x)). This proves the original existential and both equations without changing any hypotheses. The degree-zero block comparison is used only internally to verify the first differential.

theorem ringCechCoordinates_tensor_step (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (r : ℕ)
    (f : Fin (r + 1) → A)
    (K : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (a : K ⟶ ringComplexSingle A)
    (e₀ : (K.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ≃ₗ[A] A)
    (e : ∀ q : ℕ, (K.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ≃ₗ[A]
      ((t : Fin (q + 1) ↪o Fin r) → Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i).succ)))
    (l : ∀ (q : ℕ) (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r) (j : Fin (q + 2)),
      Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j i)).succ) →ₐ[A]
        Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i).succ))
    (hneg : ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (K.X n))
    (hd₀ : ∀ (x : (K.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)) (t : Fin 1 ↪o Fin r),
      e 0 ((K.d 0 1).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
        algebraMap A (Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i).succ)) (e₀ x))
    (hd : ∀ (q : ℕ) (x : (K.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))
      (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r),
      e (q + 1) ((K.d ((q : ℤ) + 1) ((q : ℤ) + 2)).val.app
          (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
        ∑ j : Fin (q + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val •
          l q t j (e q x ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j).trans t)))
    (ha : ∀ x : (K.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩),
      ringComplexAugmentationValue a x = e₀ x) :
    let O := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A
    letI : IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} (RingSiteModules A) :=
      SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian _
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory O
    letI := SheafOfModules.symmetricCategory O
    letI := Classical.choice (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed O).1
    letI := Classical.choice (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed O).2.1
    let s : (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections := ⟨fun _ ↦ f 0, fun _ ↦ rfl⟩
    let P := ringedLocalizationTwoTerm O s
    let L := HomologicalComplex.tensorObj P K
    let b : L ⟶ ringComplexSingle A :=
      HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (ringedLocalizationTwoTermAugmentation O s) a ≫
        (HomologicalComplex.leftUnitor (ringComplexSingle A)).hom
    ∃ (e : ∀ q : ℕ, (L.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ≃ₗ[A]
        ((t : Fin (q + 1) ↪o Fin (r + 1)) → Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))))
      (l : ∀ (q : ℕ) (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin (r + 1)) (j : Fin (q + 2)),
        Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j i))) →ₐ[A]
          Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))),
      (∀ (x : (L.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)) (t : Fin 1 ↪o Fin (r + 1)),
        e 0 ((L.d 0 1).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
          algebraMap A (Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i)))
            (ringComplexAugmentationValue b x)) ∧
      (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : (L.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))
        (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin (r + 1)),
        e (q + 1) ((L.d ((q : ℤ) + 1) ((q : ℤ) + 2)).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
          ∑ j : Fin (q + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val •
            l q t j (e q x ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j).trans t)))
